messages:
sam: Heads-up — we're bringing Lodestar-13B into the onboarding pipeline. LICENSE at the repo root looks like CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Quick triage: can we quantize and ship weights to customers, host as Redwood hosted API, or fine-tune and distribute derivatives? Need a short list of constraints so we don't accidentally release something.

license-bot: Detected license: CC BY-NC-ND-4.0 in /LICENSE (https://git.example.com/lodestar/LICENSE) :info:

jordan: Ran a quick int8 conversion in sandbox, perf looks decent. Command I used: ```python convert.py --model lodestar --quant int8 --out lodestar-int8.pt```
But if ND is present that seems like a hard stop for shipping modified weights, right? :thinking:

maria-legal: Short answer: CC BY-NC-ND forbids "derivative works" and commercial use. Important notes: shipping modified weights likely counts as distribution of a derivative; fine-tuning is almost certainly a derivative; NC means no commercial exploitation.

maria-legal: Hosting as an API is a gray area — some courts treat SaaS as not "distribution" but NC could still restrict commercial hosting. We need a formal review and possibly permission from the upstream authors or a commercial license.

tess: For onboarding flow: I'll add a temporary blocker that prevents any "distribute weights" step and flags license NC/ND models as "legal review required". Also we should only allow internal evals in a sandbox.

oliver: Customer asked for Dedicated deployment (reserved GPU pool) and a pinned model for low-latency. If we can't host or redistribute, we could offer to help customers self-host if they accept license terms, or request a commercial license from upstream. Fine-tuning for customers is a no-go without express permission.

jordan: To be concrete, what's the rule for providing a docker image that contains quantized weights? Is that distribution? (I assume yes.)

maria-legal: Yes, a docker image with weights is distribution. Also transforming weights (quantizing) may be treated as creating a derivative in many jurisdictions. We should assume conservatively that both are prohibited under ND.

maria-legal: Next steps from legal: I'll open a formal intake, confirm jurisdictional nuance, and reach out to upstream maintainers to request a commercial/dual license or explicit permission for: (a) hosting as a service, (b) distributing quantized weights to customers, (c) creating customer-specific fine-tuned models.

license-bot: Created ticket LEG-2026-58: "Lodestar license interpretation + upstream commercial license request" (link: https://redwood.legal/tickets/LEG-2026-58) :page_with_curl:

sam: Action items captured: 1) Legal to confirm and contact upstream (LEG-2026-58). 2) DevEx (tess) to add onboarding guardrails: block weight distribution and production release until LEG clears. 3) Eng (jordan/oliver) to keep quant/fine-tune experiments in sandbox and document commands. I'll pause the public eval run.

jordan: I'll move the quant artifacts to internal-only bucket and add a README note: "do not distribute until LEG signoff".

tess: I'll add the license check to the onboarding CI and create a short checklist item: "NC/ND -> legal review required; block weight export/distribution."

maria-legal: I'll ping upstream today and update this thread when I have a response. If they offer a dual/commercial license we can re-evaluate distribution and customer deployments.

oliver: Thanks — will notify the customer that we need to validate licensing before proceeding.

sam: Thanks all. Hold on releases, keep experiments sandboxed. :+1:

maria-legal: Posted an interim note in #eng-ml and added the LIC file to LEG ticket. Will follow up in 48-72h.
